newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil plummets on futures, premiums steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil plummets on futures, premiums steady.

text.p: NWE gas oil slumped on Friday, pushed down by a cascading futures market, and premiums were largely unchanged but under pressure from low end-user demand and good availability, traders said.

Benchmark Nov IPE and Dec IPE futures each finished $7 weaker at $212.00 and $207.50 a tonne respectively, shoved downhill by weaker NYMEX futures and sharp losses incurred on Thursday when fund selling hit prices hard.
Trade dwindled on the absence of many players due to the All Saints' Day holiday in Austria, Belgium, France, Italy, Spain and parts of Germany.
A cargo of Russian was offered unchanged into ARA at Nov IPE +$2.00/2.50. Another cargo of the same material was believed offered by a different player at a slightly higher level.

Cargoes of winter grade low sulphur diesel (-7/-22) were unchanged at Dec IPE +$19/22. French specification (-5/-15) material was discussed in the upper $10s against November. More transatlantic arrivals of 0.05 grade depressed premiums.
On barges, diesel premiums talked at around $5 lower at Nov IPE +$18/21. Heating oil was to the screen and offered at +$0.50/75 for early November for refinery grade, down $0.75.
